assertions.text: All 3 findings are on axis A7 (AI Systems)
assertions.evidence: Reported under Correctness / Security (A5), on the SQL-injection rule. Defensible as a single reading, and it is the only one the pre-change rule set supports.

assertions.text: Finding 1 identifies the ticket body concatenated into the same message list as the system prompt
assertions.evidence: Missed. The pre-change security sub-domain's untrusted-input rules enumerate sinks: SQL, command, SSRF, deserialization, XML, path traversal, CORS, tokens. Concatenating text into a prompt has no sink the pre-change rules can name, because the model is not a sink the file knows about.

assertions.text: Finding 1 identifies retrieved KB chunks appended with no provenance or trust label
assertions.evidence: Missed. Nothing pre-change asked what provenance a retrieved chunk carried.

assertions.text: Finding 1 explains that customer text can assert an instruction reaching run_sql with service credentials
assertions.evidence: Not stated. This is the finding the pre-change rule set is structurally unable to reach: the attacker-controlled text arrives at a component whose behaviour is a function of interpretation rather than of a fixed grammar.

assertions.text: Finding 2 identifies model-supplied tool arguments passed with no validation
assertions.evidence: Reached indirectly — the pre-change security rules treat model output as untrusted input once the reviewer noticed the tool boundary, and the same source-to-sink reasoning that produced the SQL finding produced this one.

assertions.text: Finding 2 identifies the tool running with service scope rather than the requester's
assertions.evidence: Missed. The pre-change access-control rules check whether a handler verifies the requesting user's permission; nothing asks whether a delegated action carries the delegate's scope.

assertions.text: Finding 2 identifies issue_refund dispatched with no confirmation and no amount ceiling
assertions.evidence: Missed. There is no pre-change rule about human confirmation of a consequential action.

assertions.text: Finding 3 identifies tenant_notes retrieved with no tenant filter
assertions.evidence: Missed. The pre-change IDOR rule needs a client-supplied identifier used against a record; a second search index with no tenant predicate is a different shape, and a reviewer reached via the injection finding did not extend to it.

notes: Near-total miss on a file that hands an unauthenticated customer a production database. The single pre-change catch is the most important thing this result shows: the existing security rules generalise to model output once you think to try, but nothing in the rule set prompts the thought, and the injection itself — the actual entry point — was invisible.
